subject: lion
pitch: A proud old lion resting with his head held high. A huge shaggy mane fading from golden blond at the face to dark chocolate at the edges, a tawny body with a pale cream belly and muzzle, amber eyes, a broad black nose, a scar across one eyebrow, big padded paws and a long tail ending in a dark tuft.

I'm planning to build a single TypeScript module using the SDK for a lion in a resting pose — body lying with legs tucked under and head raised, using realistic proportions like a shoulder height around 1.2m and body length near 2.5m.

Now I'm mapping out the API: setting up joints and a chain for the skeleton, then adding parts and sweeps for the body, tail, and mane. I'm thinking the mane could be built from clustered sphere shapes with a gradient paint fading from golden-blond near the head to deeper chocolate tones outward, giving it a shaggy, layered look.

Now I'm sketching the overall pose: a sphinx-like resting lion facing forward, with the body sweeping from hips to chest at specific heights and radii, built as a spine chain so joints can later be posed.

I'm defining the joint hierarchy next—root at the pelvis, a spine chain running up through the torso, and a neck chain continuing from the chest up to the head base, each with path points mapping out the lion's rising posture.

For the head and jaw I'm placing a head joint parented to the last neck joint, aimed forward, plus a small jaw joint beneath it for the mouth. Then I'm working out the front leg chains for a resting pose—shoulder, elbow, and wrist points positioned so the forearms lie flat on the ground ahead of the chest.

Now I'm defining leg sweeps using tapered radius tubes along each limb chain, naming the joints so span counts match, and starting on the hind legs folded into a lying position with the thigh angled forward-down and the shin tucked back toward the paw.

I'm setting similar four-point chains for the front legs with named joints for shoulder, elbow, wrist, and paw, mirroring these across the x-axis for the opposite side, and now beginning the tail chain curving back from the pelvis along the ground toward a dark tuft at the tip.

For the head, I'm placing a sphere skull with a cream muzzle, black nose, amber eyes, a scar mark, and small ears, then positioning the mane as a ring of spheres around the head, generated with a random angle sweep that skips the front face.

Then I'm laying out a neck chain running from the end of the spine up toward a head joint angled forward and slightly up, with a tapering radius profile matching the mane coverage, reusing the body's tawny countershade paint for the neck sweep.
